VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS
Sales Training Call — Speaker Notes

Date: September 27, 2021
Prepared by: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
Subject: Answering the Metal Ion Question — Training Notes

These notes support the September 30 field call. Please use the approved language as written where possible. The objective is to be responsive and credible without making clinical interpretations in the field.

Slide 1 — Opening

“Surgeons are seeing more questions around cobalt and chromium testing generally, including from patients who have read about metal-on-metal hips. Our role is to acknowledge the question, explain the information available in the product labeling, and connect the physician with the appropriate Veridian clinical resource when interpretation is needed.”

Do not characterize a patient’s result as normal, abnormal, concerning, or unrelated to the implant. Do not compare one patient’s value to another patient’s value.

Slide 2 — If asked: “Do ApexHip patients have elevated ions?”

Suggested response:

“Cobalt and chromium ion monitoring is an established topic across metal-on-metal hip systems and should be considered by the treating physician in the context of the individual patient. ApexHip labeling addresses follow-up and clinical evaluation considerations. We are in the process of implementing an updated label to provide additional clarity for surgeons.”

Avoid: “Apex does not cause elevated ions,” “the levels are harmless,” or “this is expected.”

If a surgeon asks whether ApexHip is the cause of a particular lab result, say:

“I can’t interpret an individual laboratory value or determine causation. I can connect you with Medical Affairs so the appropriate clinical discussion can occur.”

Route all lab-value, imaging, revision, pseudotumor, tissue-reaction, or causation questions to Medical Affairs. Do not collect or summarize clinical details by text message. Follow the complaint intake procedure if the surgeon is reporting a potential product complaint.

Slide 3 — Registry question / March 2021 NJR data

The March 2021 NJR annual report includes a five-year ApexHip revision rate of 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average. Do not dispute the figure, speculate about registry methodology, or provide your own explanation for the difference.

Approved framing:

“The published registry figures should be viewed in the context of broader industry variance, including patient selection, surgeon practice, follow-up patterns, and differences in reporting populations. Regulatory has reviewed the language we are using, and the updated labeling will provide additional information for clinicians.”

If pressed, repeat the published figures accurately and offer to arrange a discussion with Medical Affairs or Post-Market Surveillance. Do not say that the rate is “within normal range” or that it is “not statistically meaningful.”

Slide 4 — Label update

“The label update is in progress. It is intended to give surgeons clearer follow-up information and does not change the need for physicians to exercise their independent clinical judgment.”

Do not provide an expected approval or release date. Do not distribute draft label language.

Slide 5 — Keeping product messaging distinct

KneeFlex may be used as a simple example of product-specific messaging: “KneeFlex is a different platform and does not involve the same metal-on-metal bearing discussion.” Do not broaden that statement into a comparative safety claim or suggest that no KneeFlex issues have ever been reported.

Close with: “Be calm, be factual, and escalate clinical interpretation. We earn trust by not overreaching.”

MERIDIAN TESTING LABS
Biomechanical Evaluation Services
1180 Research Park Drive, Indianapolis, Indiana 46202

14 August 2019

To: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.
4400 Silver Lake Blvd
Warsaw, Indiana 46580

Subject: ISO 14242 Wear Test Report – ApexHip Supplemental Inclination Study

Dear Mr. Halvorsen:

At Veridian Orthopedics’ request, Meridian Testing Labs conducted a supplemental simulator wear study of the ApexHip metal-on-metal total hip bearing under elevated acetabular cup inclination. This work was requested as an extension of the previously completed ISO 14242 protocol testing conducted at the standard 45-degree cup orientation.

Study Objective
The objective was to compare volumetric wear, visual bearing surface condition, and cobalt/chromium release rates for ApexHip constructs tested at 55 degrees inclination against the established 45-degree control configuration.

Test Articles
Six ApexHip bearing constructs were evaluated. Test articles consisted of Co/Cr acetabular cups from the V-2100 series and matching Co/Cr femoral heads from the H-3050 series. The cup lots included V-2108, V-2113, and V-2121; head lots included H-3052, H-3057, and H-3061. Components were supplied by Veridian and inspected upon receipt for packaging integrity and visible defects. No pre-test anomalies were observed.

Methodology
Testing was performed using six-station hip joint simulators in accordance with ISO 14242 loading and motion profiles, except for the specified acetabular orientation. Three stations were configured at 45 degrees inclination and served as controls. Three stations were configured at 55 degrees inclination. All stations were operated for 5 million cycles at 1 Hz under bovine serum lubricant diluted to 25 g/L total protein concentration. Lubricant was changed at 0.5 million-cycle intervals.

Gravimetric measurements were taken at each lubricant interval after cleaning and drying pursuant to laboratory procedure MTL-WEAR-014. Lubricant samples were retained at each interval and analyzed by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry for cobalt and chromium content. Bearing surfaces were examined by optical microscopy at completion.

Results
The 45-degree control group demonstrated cumulative volumetric wear consistent with prior ApexHip simulator work. The 55-degree group showed a material increase beginning between 1.0 and 1.5 million cycles, with the differential increasing through the end of the study.

| Configuration | Mean Cumulative Wear at 5M Cycles | Mean Co/Cr Release Rate |
|---|---:|---:|
| 45-degree inclination | 14.2 mm³ | 0.18 mg/million cycles |
| 55-degree inclination | 71.6 mm³ | 0.94 mg/million cycles |

The elevated-inclination group therefore exhibited approximately five times the volumetric wear and metal ion release rate observed in the 45-degree control group. Two of three 55-degree stations also demonstrated localized polishing and stripe wear near the superior rim of the cup, consistent with edge-loading contact. These features were not observed to the same extent in the control group.

Conclusion
Under the conditions tested, elevated cup inclination materially increased wear of the ApexHip metal-on-metal bearing. Clinical cup positioning above approximately 50 degrees inclination presents an elevated risk of edge loading, increased wear volume, and increased cobalt/chromium release relative to the standard 45-degree orientation.

This report is provided to Mr. Halvorsen for internal distribution to the Veridian design team. It should be considered together with the applicable design inputs, risk analysis, and clinical evaluation materials.

Sincerely,

Meridian Testing Labs

Elaine Porter, Ph.D.
Director, Biomechanical Evaluation Services

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
Quarterly All-Hands Presentation Notes
Speaker: Rob Castellano, Chief Executive Officer
Date: April 22, 2019
Subject: Company Direction 2019

Slide 1 — Opening

Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time today, whether you are here at the Hub, joining from Cork, or listening in from one of our regional offices.

We had a strong first quarter. That is because of the work being done across this company: on the manufacturing floor, in the labs, in Quality and Regulatory, in the field, and in every function that supports our customers. Our direction for 2019 is straightforward: grow responsibly, invest where we can win, and keep earning the confidence surgeons and patients place in us.

Slide 2 — Growth Strategy

We are not pursuing growth for its own sake. We are concentrating our investment in joint reconstruction, where Veridian has credibility, experienced people, and a real opportunity to improve patient mobility.

That means continuing to build our hip portfolio, bringing KneeFlex to market the right way, and expanding our capacity without compromising the operating discipline that got us here. We will be selective in our investments, but we will not be timid.

Slide 3 — Cork Expansion

A significant part of that investment is the expansion of our Cork facility. Cork has become an increasingly important manufacturing and engineering center for Veridian, and the additional space will support higher-volume production as well as the teams responsible for advanced surface technologies.

The project is moving forward in phases. Bill and the Cork team have done a tremendous job planning around current production needs, and I want to recognize the cross-functional work required to keep the line running while we build for the future.

Slide 4 — Denver Office

We have also signed a lease for a new Denver office. This gives us a stronger base in the Mountain West and a better place for our commercial, clinical, and customer-support teams to work with surgeons in that region.

Denver is not just an address. It is part of our effort to be closer to customers and to recruit the talent we need as our business grows.

Slide 5 — KneeFlex

CORRECTIVE AND PREVENTIVE ACTION FORM

CAPA No.: CAPA-2022-0091
Title: Plasma Spray Chamber Maintenance Verification
Date Opened: 12 Jul 2022
Site/Department: Cork Manufacturing / Operations
Product: ApexHip Acetabular Cup — KinetiCoat
Related Recall: FDA Recall No. Z-1418-2022
Affected Lots: V-2200 through V-2299

1. PROBLEM DESCRIPTION

Incoming inspection reports were received from Northgate Health System and a Denver hospital identifying visible flaking/delamination of KinetiCoat porous titanium coating on ApexHip cups upon removal from sterile packaging. Initial lot tracing identified cups manufactured in Cork between November 2021 and February 2022, within lots V-2200 through V-2299.

The condition presents a potential risk that coating adhesion may be inadequate for intended bone ingrowth. Distribution of affected product was stopped and the voluntary field action was initiated on 14 June 2022. A total of 1,140 units were distributed; implant status is being tracked separately through the recall file.

2. INVESTIGATION / ROOT CAUSE

Review of batch records, chamber logs, maintenance records, and retained samples identified a plasma-spray parameter drift following chamber maintenance performed in November 2021. The maintenance work included replacement and realignment of chamber components. The existing maintenance procedure required return-to-service documentation but did not require verification using a coated coupon, nor did it define acceptance criteria for confirmation of spray parameters after maintenance.

The line was returned to production based on equipment operational checks only. Subsequent review indicates that the chamber operated outside the validated parameter range for coating deposition consistency. This resulted in reduced KinetiCoat adhesion on affected cup lots.

3. CORRECTIVE ACTIONS

a. Revise WI-CORK-PS-014, “Plasma Spray Chamber Maintenance and Restart,” to require a documented maintenance verification checklist before production release.

b. Require post-maintenance coupon testing for each chamber maintenance event affecting torch, powder feed, gas flow, chamber alignment, or control settings. Coupon results must meet approved adhesion acceptance criteria before product manufacture may resume.

c. Add Quality approval to the restart checklist. Manufacturing may not release the chamber based solely on Operations sign-off.

d. Retrain Plasma Spray Operators, Maintenance, Manufacturing Engineering, and Quality personnel on the revised procedure. Training records will be maintained in the Cork training file.

4. PREVENTIVE ACTIONS

The revised checklist will be applied to both plasma-spray chambers at Cork. Maintenance work orders will include a mandatory Quality hold point. A monthly review of chamber maintenance and coupon-test records will be conducted by the Cork Quality Manager for the first six months following implementation.

5. EFFECTIVENESS CHECK PLAN

Adhesion testing will be performed on production samples from the first three post-restart lots following any qualifying maintenance event. Results will be reviewed against established specification limits and compared with pre-maintenance baseline data. No repeat coating flaking complaints, nonconforming inspection findings, or adhesion failures are acceptable during the effectiveness-check period.

Effectiveness review due: 31 Oct 2022
CAPA closure requires Quality approval.

TO: File (Workday Case Ref: INV-2021-089)
FROM: Lisa Tran, HR Business Partner – R&D and Quality
DATE: January 20, 2022
SUBJECT: Hotline Investigation Summary – Report H-2021-047

1. BACKGROUND & SCOPE
On November 18, 2021, an anonymous report was submitted via the Veridian Ethics Hotline (Ref # H-2021-047) alleging that personnel within the Quality and Complaint Handling department were deliberately suppressing adverse event complaint trending related to the ApexHip system. Specifically, the reporter alleged that metal-on-metal wear and metallosis/ARMD complaint rates were intentionally slow-walked or reclassified in TrackWise to avoid triggering premature internal regulatory escalation and external mandatory reporting.

Human Resources initiated a formal internal inquiry in coordination with the Legal department. Over the past seven weeks, investigative interviews were conducted with seven current employees across Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, and Regulatory Affairs, including Complaint Handling Specialists, Post-Market Analysts, and department leadership. A review of relevant TrackWise escalation workflows, standard operating procedures (SOP-QA-402, SOP-RA-110), and internal correspondence was also performed.

2. INVESTIGATION FINDINGS
Based on the totality of interview statements and contemporaneous records, the investigation concludes that there is no substantiated evidence of intentional or malicious suppression of complaint data or adverse event trending by Quality leadership or individual complaint specialists.

However, the inquiry identified material process vulnerabilities and cross-functional communication breakdowns:
* Documentation Gaps: Escalation discussions between Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling) and Dana Okonkwo’s Regulatory Affairs team frequently occurred via informal verbal touchpoints or ad hoc check-ins rather than structured, formal TrackWise or Agile escalation records. This lack of formal audit-trail documentation gave junior team members the perception that concerns were being dismissed or stalled.
* Procedural Ambiguity: While individual adverse event MDR determinations adhered strictly to 21 CFR 803 decision trees per procedure, thresholds for aggregate "out-of-trend" statistical escalations were inconsistently understood between the primary complaint handlers and post-market surveillance.

3. RECOMMENDATIONS & OUTCOMES
1. Managerial Coaching: HR will implement targeted leadership and communication coaching for Priya Raman. Coaching will focus on transparent downward communication, structured upward handoffs, and reinforcing psychological safety within her reporting chain so team members do not feel compelled to seek anonymous escalation channels.
2. Process Alignment & Training: Quality and Regulatory Affairs must jointly update the interface SOP governing complaint trending escalations. Mandatory retraining will be assigned in Workday Learning for all Quality complaint-handling staff before end of Q1 2022.
3. Legal Coordination: In light of anticipated litigation exposure regarding ApexHip performance and registry data, this investigation summary and associated interview memoranda have been shared with Elena Ruiz at Whitfield & Barr LLP.

This matter is considered closed from an internal HR workplace conduct standpoint, pending execution of the corrective coaching and process actions noted above.

Subject: Kessler Reid Newsletter - Design Trends in Medical Marketing 2021

Happy New Year from Kessler Reid.

As healthcare organizations look ahead to 2021, we are seeing a continued move toward cleaner, calmer visual systems across patient and professional collateral. The past year has made clarity and confidence more important than ever; audiences want information that is easy to scan without feeling cold or overly clinical.

A few design trends our studio is watching:

• Warm minimalism. Neutral backgrounds paired with one confident accent color continue to replace dense, multi-color layouts.

• Human-centered photography. Authentic settings and natural expressions are outperforming heavily staged stock imagery, particularly in patient-facing materials.

• Typography with personality. Modern sans serif families remain the workhorse, but brands are introducing more distinctive type treatments for headlines. Larger type and generous spacing also improve readability across print and digital formats.

• Accessible color palettes. Deep blues, soft greens, muted terracottas, and high-contrast neutrals are appearing frequently. Accessibility review should remain part of every creative process, not an end-stage check.

• Modular content. Flexible page components allow a brochure, landing page, email, and social asset to feel connected while serving different reading behaviors.

We expect the strongest healthcare work this year will balance clinical credibility with a more approachable, optimistic visual tone.

Best,
Kessler Reid Creative Team

QUALITY & COMPLAINT HANDLING MEMORANDUM

Date: June 22, 2020
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Subject: KneeFlex Complaint Trend Summary Q2 2020

This memorandum summarizes complaint activity for the KneeFlex Total Knee System through June 15, 2020, including complaints received from April 1 through June 15 and year-to-date trend review. The analysis was completed in accordance with QP-820-014, Complaint Handling and Medical Device Reporting, using closed and open TrackWise records as of the extraction date.

Q2 Complaint Summary

A total of 23 KneeFlex complaints were received during the review period. Following duplicate review and preliminary coding, the principal categories are as follows:

| Complaint category | Q2 reports | Initial assessment |
|---|---:|---|
| Tibial tray loosening | 11 | Under clinical/product review; no common lot, size, or surgical site trend identified |
| Polyethylene wear debris | 4 | Consistent with known long-term wear profile; all cases involve patient/surgical factors requiring follow-up |
| Instrument breakage during surgery | 2 | Instrument complaints; contained to two separate procedural sets |
| Other / incomplete information | 6 | Pending additional records, product return, or closure as non-product related |

The eleven tibial tray loosening reports remain the largest category by count. Quality reviewed available implant duration, surgeon narratives, radiographs where supplied, and lot information. The cases are distributed across multiple tray sizes and manufacturing lots. At this time, the available information does not establish a recurring device failure mode. Several reports identify alignment, fixation technique, patient weight, or prior bone quality concerns as possible contributing factors, although those factors should not be treated as final conclusions until the clinical review is complete.

The four wear-debris reports have been routed for routine review with Post-Market Surveillance. Reported time to presentation is within the range anticipated for the relevant patient population and does not indicate an acute or unexpected increase. The two intraoperative instrument breakage reports have been sent to Operations for return analysis; neither involved a retained fragment or report of patient injury.

Complaint rates remain within the expected range when compared with available predicate-device complaint experience and KneeFlex’s current distribution base. There is no statistically meaningful increase in report frequency for the quarter, and no clustering by customer, geography, lot, or surgeon has been identified. No new MDR trend has been identified from this review. Individual event reporting decisions will continue to be made per procedure and documented in the associated TrackWise record.

Disposition

No CAPA is warranted this quarter. Quality will continue routine monthly surveillance of tibial tray loosening reports and will reassess if additional information identifies a common failure mechanism, a lot association, or a material change in rate. The instrument return analyses will be reviewed upon completion and included in the next quarterly trend package.

Please retain this memorandum with the Q2 PMS materials. Questions on specific records should be directed to Quality before any external characterization is made.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

*Footnote: The complaint-handling workflow used for KneeFlex follows the same TrackWise intake process used for ApexHip under QP-820-014; this reference concerns procedure only and does not incorporate ApexHip complaint information into this analysis.*

SUBJECT: ClassicHip Finished Goods Inventory Aging & Proposed Write-Down Analysis

Owen,

Per our discussion last week regarding the continued operational phase-out of the ClassicHip system, I have finalized the aging analysis of our remaining finished-goods inventory held across Warsaw central distribution and the four regional hubs (Atlanta, Dallas, Denver, Newark).

Given that commercial demand for ClassicHip has dropped another 42% year-over-year as surgical volume transitioned away from metal-on-polyethylene lines, our current inventory levels significantly exceed projected trailing demand through the scheduled 2022 product retirement date.

RECALL EFFECTIVENESS CHECK REPORT — ROUND 2 SUMMARY
FDA Recall Number: Z-1418-2022
Product: ApexHip Acetabular Cup, Lots V-2200 through V-2299

Date: September 12, 2022
Prepared by: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Distribution: Dana Okonkwo (VP Regulatory Affairs); Bill Kowalski (Plant Manager, Cork)

1. PURPOSE

Per procedure QSP-806-04 and the recordkeeping requirements of 21 CFR 806, this report documents the second-round effectiveness check for the voluntary Class II recall initiated June 14, 2022, covering ApexHip acetabular cup lots V-2200–V-2299 (1,140 units distributed).

2. SUMMARY OF FINDINGS

As of the close of the Round 2 verification window (September 9, 2022), field accountability stands as follows:

- Total units distributed: 1,140
- Units accounted for: 1,094 (96.0%)
- Confirmed implanted (per hospital/ASC attestation): 412
- Units returned to Veridian or confirmed destroyed on-site: 682
- Units remaining untraced: 46 (4.0%)

This represents an improvement over the Round 1 check (July 2022), which accounted for approximately 88% of distributed units. Per procedure, a third round is not automatically required once accountability exceeds 95%, but given the number of small accounts still outstanding, I am recommending continued targeted follow-up rather than closing the file at this time.

3. OUTSTANDING UNITS

The 46 untraced units are concentrated at two accounts, both smaller ambulatory surgical centers rather than hospital systems:

- Crestview Ambulatory Surgical Center (approx. 27 units unaccounted)
- Lakeside Same-Day Surgery Center (approx. 19 units unaccounted)

Both accounts received the original June 14 recall notification and a follow-up letter dated July 28. Neither has returned a completed accountability form as of this writing. Field sales (Southeast region) has been asked to assist in obtaining direct confirmation from purchasing/materials management contacts at each site, since phone follow-up from Quality has not been productive.

4. ROOT CAUSE STATUS

Root cause for the coating adhesion nonconformance remains as previously reported: plasma-spray parameter drift following a chamber maintenance event at the Cork facility, affecting the KinetiCoat application process for the subject lot range. This is documented in CAPA-2022-0091, which remains open pending completion of the effectiveness check and closure of associated corrective actions (chamber requalification protocol, revised post-maintenance verification step). Bill, per our last conversation I don't believe there's anything further needed from the Cork line for this report, but please let me know if the CAPA team wants updated batch records referenced here.

5. RECOMMENDATION

I recommend:

(a) Issuing a second follow-up letter to Crestview and Lakeside within 10 business days, with a copy to Regional Sales for in-person follow-up;
(b) Continuing to log all accountability responses in TrackWise under the existing recall record;
(c) Deferring a Round 3 effectiveness check determination until the outcome of item (a) is known, currently targeted for review by October 15, 2022.

Please let me know if either of you has questions or wants this escalated to Regulatory for direct account contact.

Priya

Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2021 09:41:05 -0500
Subject: RE: Early look at 2021 NJR data ahead of March report

Greg, Dana,

Thank you for flagging this early. A 7.1% five-year revision rate is certainly a figure that will command attention from both the registry steering group and our European surgeons.

We must exercise standard clinical caution before drawing definitive conclusions from aggregate registry data. Revision disparities frequently reflect confounding variables, particularly patient selection criteria (e.g., higher activity profiles in younger cohorts) or variable surgical technique across centers, rather than intrinsic device design flaws alone.

That said, the biomechanical mechanism Tom Halvorsen described regarding micro-separation and edge loading at steeper acetabular cup inclination angles (55°+) is entirely biologically plausible. If high-angle placement generates localized wear stripes and accelerated metal ion release, early adverse local tissue reactions would clinically manifest right around the 3- to 5-year mark.

We should not attempt to dissect this piecemeal. Once the NJR tables are finalized next month, I recommend convening a formal joint Clinical-Regulatory-Quality review meeting to examine the explant data, registry sub-cohorts, and our current IFU.

Best regards,

Leon

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
MEETING MINUTES

Meeting: Quarterly Registry Review — Q4 2021 Update
Date: January 10, 2022
Time: 10:00–11:00 AM ET
Location: Hub, Conference Room 2B / Teams hybrid
Minutes prepared by: Devon Mitchell

Attendees: Greg Novak (Post-Market Surveillance), Dana Okonkwo (Regulatory Affairs), Priya Raman (Quality & Complaint Handling), Dr. Leon Adeyemi (CMO)

1. Purpose
This meeting was a scheduled follow-up to the September 14, 2021 Registry Signal Review, to check whether newer registry data changes the picture that led to the decision to continue selling ApexHip with the labeling update and October 2021 Dear Doctor letter.

2. AJRR Q4 2021 Data (Novak)
Novak presented late-2021 AJRR figures. Revision rates for ApexHip remain elevated relative to the broader class average, consistent in direction and magnitude with the March 2021 NJR finding of a 7.1% five-year revision rate versus a 3.2% class average. Novak noted the AJRR dataset has a shorter follow-up window than NJR but the trend line is not moving in a favorable direction quarter over quarter. He cautioned against over-reading a single quarter but said two consecutive registries now point the same way.

3. Discussion — Is the Current Response Sufficient?
Okonkwo asked whether the label update and surgeon letter constitute an adequate response given the AJRR confirmation, or whether the company should revisit a design change (referencing the ECO-2019-118 proposal that was deferred in 2019) or a temporary sales pause pending further analysis.

Raman noted that complaint volumes in TrackWise have not shown a corresponding spike since the Dear Doctor letter went out, but acknowledged this could reflect underreporting or a lag rather than resolution.

Adeyemi stated that from a clinical standpoint the registry signal is concerning but that causation relative to surgical technique (inclination angle) versus device design has not been definitively separated, and that a sales pause is a significant step that should not be taken on registry data alone without further wear-testing correlation.

There was general discussion of the anticipated litigation hold, expected to be entered February 1, 2022, following Whitfield & Barr's engagement in January. The group agreed this development increases the importance of being able to show the company is actively monitoring and reassessing, but did not treat it as changing the substantive risk analysis.

4. Decision
No decision was made to alter the current course of action. The label update and Dear Doctor letter remain the company's position for now. The group agreed to revisit at the next quarterly review or sooner if AJRR or NJR data worsens materially.

5. Action Items
- Novak to prepare updated registry trend charts (NJR/AJRR combined view) for inclusion in the next board pre-read.
- Raman to continue monthly complaint trending and flag any deviation.
- Next meeting to be scheduled for early April 2022.

Minutes distributed to attendees only.

URGENT: IMPORTANT MEDICAL DEVICE INFORMATION
ApexHip Total Hip System (510(k) K162447)

Dear Orthopedic Surgeon:

The purpose of this letter is to provide updated clinical management recommendations regarding the Veridian Orthopedics ApexHip Total Hip System (cleared via 510(k) K162447 in March 2017). Veridian Orthopedics is committed to patient safety and continuous evaluation of post-market clinical performance.

Recent analyses of international and domestic joint replacement registries, including the National Joint Registry (NJR) of the United Kingdom and late 2021 observational subsets from the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR), have identified an elevated cumulative revision rate for the ApexHip system compared to historical polyethylene bearing benchmarks. Specifically, data indicate a 5-year cumulative revision rate trending higher than aggregate registry class averages, with an increased risk profile observed in implant cohorts utilizing larger femoral head diameters (44 mm to 50 mm) and in constructs where the acetabular cup component was positioned at higher inclination angles (exceeding 45 degrees).

In light of these post-market registry trends, Veridian Orthopedics recommends the following enhanced clinical monitoring protocols:

1. Routine Clinical Follow-Up: Schedule regular follow-up examinations for all implanted ApexHip patients at minimum annual intervals, regardless of current symptomatic presentation.
2. Cross-Sectional Imaging and Ion Testing: For patients presenting with persistent pain, unexplained groin discomfort, swelling, or mechanical clicking, perform cross-sectional imaging (such as MARS-MRI or high-resolution ultrasound) to evaluate for adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR/ARMD) and obtain serum cobalt and chromium ion concentration panels.
3. Component Evaluation: When assessing imaging, verify acetabular orientation and cup abduction angles to detect potential edge-loading phenomena.

Surgeons should continue to report any adverse events, unexpected revisions, or suspected tissue necrosis directly to Veridian Quality & Complaint Handling at complaints@veridianortho.com or via our medical safety hotline at 1-800-555-0194, which routes directly into our TrackWise complaint intake and regulatory surveillance system.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

TO: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs; Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling; Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer
FROM: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
DATE: September 20, 2021
SUBJECT: ApexHip System Instructions for Use (IFU) — Proposed Labeling Revision Rationale & Drafting

Following the consensus reached during the September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, this memorandum outlines the commercial and clinical positioning rationale for the proposed updates to the ApexHip Acetabular Cup Instructions for Use (IFU-0144, Rev. D) and the associated Surgical Technique Guide.

1. Strategic Context & Objective
Recent registry publications (notably the 2021 NJR Annual Report indicating a 7.1% cumulative revision rate at 5 years) require clear risk-mitigation measures from the manufacturer. However, as discussed with senior leadership, our objective is to provide actionable clinical instruction to operating surgeons that accounts for these registry trends while avoiding an overbroad safety communication or market action that could inadvertently undermine commercial confidence in the Apex platform.

By framing wear performance around strict anatomical placement parameters, we can reinforce optimal surgical execution and address the underlying registry signal without triggering broader market alarm.

2. Proposed IFU Revisions (Section 4: Warnings and Precautions)
We propose adding the following language under Section 4.2 (*Implant Positioning and Wear Performance*):

> *"CAUTION: Clinical outcomes and bearing couple wear characteristics are highly sensitive to acetabular component orientation. Internal bench testing demonstrates that cup abduction (inclination) angles exceeding 45 degrees, particularly when combined with excessive anteversion, lead to localized edge-loading and significantly accelerated volumetric wear rates. Surgeons should verify intraoperative cup orientation using radiographic or navigational alignment aids to maintain an inclination target of 40° to 45°."*

Drafting Note: While this text directly incorporates findings from our internal bench testing regarding high-angle biomechanics, the wording intentionally characterizes this as an operative technique optimization rather than an inherent product limitation.

3. Surgical Technique Guide Additions
We will simultaneously issue an addendum to the ApexHip Surgical Technique Guide emphasizing:
- Verification of the "safe zone" (Lewinnek criteria) prior to final cup impaction.
- Specific warnings regarding patient anatomy variations (e.g., pelvic tilt in high-flexion activities) that can artificially elevate the functional inclination angle beyond 45°.

4. Alignment with Planned Communications
This labeling update will serve as the technical foundation for the upcoming "Dear Healthcare Provider" letter scheduled for release in mid-October 2021. By establishing that elevated wear is predominantly driven by component positioning outside the validated envelope, the communication appropriately shifts focus to surgical precision and patient selection.

5. Next Steps and Action Required
Per design change procedures, this revision will be routed under an expedited Change Order in Agile.

Dana — I would appreciate your formal regulatory sign-off on the proposed language above by Friday, September 24, so that Marketing and Regulatory can finalize the October Dear Doctor communication draft and confirm filing requirements under 21 CFR 803 / 820 before distribution.

MEMORANDUM

CONFIDENTIAL - HR INTERNAL ONLY

TO: Executive Leadership Team
FROM: Lisa Tran, HR Business Partner, R&D and Quality
DATE: February 5, 2024
SUBJECT: Workforce Transition Plan - ApexHip Market Withdrawal

Following the February 2, 2024 announcement regarding the voluntary global market withdrawal of the ApexHip Total Hip System, Human Resources has finalized the workforce transition and organizational alignment plan.

While this market action impacts product line revenue and commercial focus, our regulatory, clinical, and quality obligations for previously implanted units remain fully active. Consequently, this plan balances necessary commercial consolidation with targeted personnel retention across technical operations.

1. Scope of Impacted Personnel

The withdrawal directly impacts positions dedicated exclusively to the commercialization, promotional positioning, and field support of ApexHip:

• Commercial Sales: Five (5) Regional Reconstruction Specialists whose sole portfolio assignment was ApexHip conversion accounts across the Southeast, Central, and Western territories. General reconstructive sales representatives carrying KneeFlex and shoulder lines will absorb remaining territory accounts and are unaffected by this reduction.
• Marketing Communications: Four (4) dedicated contractor roles within MarCom supporting Apex product campaigns, digital asset management, and agency liaison work (Kessler Reid deliverables). Contracts will be concluded effective February 29, 2024, per standard notice provisions.
• Operations / Field Inventory: Two (2) logistics coordinator roles in Warsaw supporting hospital consignment retrieval and field kit balancing.

2. Retention of Core Technical, Quality, and Regulatory Staff

It is critical to emphasize that no headcount reductions will occur within Product Development, Regulatory Affairs, Post-Market Surveillance, or Quality Complaint Handling.

Per 21 CFR 820 and 803 requirements, our post-market surveillance, adverse event trending, and complaint investigation responsibilities continue indefinitely for all legacy implanted ApexHip systems. The following teams will remain intact:

• Quality & Complaint Handling: Priya Raman’s team will maintain current staffing levels to manage incoming TrackWise complaint files, MDR determinations, and explant evaluations.
• Post-Market Surveillance: Greg Novak will continue overseeing registry monitoring (AJRR, NJR), signal detection, and ongoing surveillance reports.
• R&D Engineering: Lead sustaining engineer Wei Chen and supporting mechanical testing staff will remain fully allocated to ongoing retrieval analyses, wear simulator evaluations, and technical support for ongoing regulatory inquiries.

3. Severance and Transition Package Terms

For eligible regular full-time employees subject to position elimination, Veridian will offer standard severance packages structured as follows:

• Base Severance: Two (2) weeks of base pay per year of continuous service, with a minimum of eight (8) weeks and a maximum of twenty-six (26) weeks.
• Benefits Continuation: Employer-subsidized COBRA premium coverage corresponding to the severance duration period.
• Incentive Compensation: Pro-rated FY2024 target bonus payouts calculated through March 31, 2024.
• Outplacement Services: Three (3) months of executive and professional outplacement assistance via Lee Hecht Harrison (LHH).

4. Implementation Timeline

• Feb 5–Feb 9: Finalize Workday role status updates; prepare individualized separation documentation and release agreements with outside legal review.
• Feb 12–Feb 16: Manager briefing sessions; coordinate notification scheduling with VP Sales Marcus Lee and relevant regional directors.
• Feb 19–Feb 23: Conduct individual notification meetings with impacted commercial staff.
• Feb 29: Contract conclusion date for MarCom external contractors.
• March 29, 2024: Target final separation date for impacted regular employees.

Please direct any questions regarding specific employee conversations or Workday processing directly to me.

AEGIS SPECIALTY INSURANCE COMPANY
Claims & Coverage Counsel
One Harbor Plaza, Suite 1400
Hartford, Connecticut 06103

February 12, 2024

VIA EMAIL AND FIRST-CLASS MAIL

Rachel Steinberg
General Counsel
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.
4400 Silver Lake Blvd
Warsaw, Indiana 46580

Re: Supplemental Reservation of Rights - ApexHip Claims
    Policy No. AEG-PL-88471; Notice of Circumstance dated September 2022

Dear Ms. Steinberg:

This letter supplements Aegis Specialty Insurance Company's reservation of rights letter dated September 30, 2022, regarding claims arising from the ApexHip hip system. That reservation remains in full force and effect, and nothing in this letter should be construed as a waiver of any right or defense set forth therein.

We understand Veridian publicly announced a voluntary market withdrawal of ApexHip on February 2, 2024. In light of that development, and the continued growth in the number of claims alleging elevated cobalt/chromium ion levels and adverse reaction to metal debris, Aegis is now reviewing whether these claims constitute a single "products hazard" occurrence subject to the policy's aggregate limit, or whether they should instead be evaluated as separate occurrences subject to per-occurrence limits. As you are aware, the distinction may materially affect the amount of coverage available to Veridian for this matter, and we want to flag this issue for you as early as possible.

To assist our continuing evaluation, we request the following within two weeks of this letter:

1. An updated count of pending and threatened ApexHip-related claims, including the MDL matters;
2. Veridian's current reserve figure for Apex-related exposure; and
3. A call with you and Owen Park to discuss claim trends and the aggregation question.

Please have your office contact the undersigned to schedule the call at your earliest convenience.

Very truly yours,

Diane Hollis
Senior Coverage Counsel
Aegis Specialty Insurance Company

Priya, Dana—

Following up on last week’s Registry Signal Review, I completed the Q3 AJRR pull using the same inclusion criteria we discussed: primary ApexHip procedures with at least 24 months of follow-up, compared with the available peer metal-on-metal cohort.

The AJRR data corroborate the direction of the March NJR findings. The absolute numbers are smaller and the confidence intervals are wider than NJR, but Apex is showing an elevated all-cause revision rate relative to peer MoM systems in the AJRR extract. The separation is most apparent in the 36–60 month follow-up band.

A few points from the stratification:

- The revision signal appears concentrated in the larger head sizes, particularly 44–50 mm. Smaller-head cases do not show the same degree of separation, although the case counts are limited.
- Where cup inclination was available in the registry record, revised Apex cases were disproportionately represented above approximately 50 degrees.
- That pattern is directionally consistent with Tom Halvorsen’s 2019 high-inclination wear work. I am not suggesting the registry establishes causation; it does, however, make the edge-loading hypothesis difficult to dismiss as a laboratory-only finding.
- Revision indications remain variably coded. Pain, elevated metal ions, adverse local tissue reaction, and “other mechanical” are all present, so I would avoid relying on any single indication category without chart-level review.

I have attached the summary workbook, including the denominator definitions, exclusions, and a tab showing the inclination/head-size subset. I also included the NJR figures for reference, but did not combine the registries analytically.

Please let me know whether you want the underlying case-level list routed to Quality for complaint cross-checking. My recommendation remains that we maintain a recurring monthly review through the label-update period rather than wait for the next annual registry publication.

Greg

Attached: Apex_Revenue_Impact_Model_Q4_2022_v5.xlsx

Owen,

Per our discussion, I refreshed the Apex model using September actuals and the current field forecast. The model is intended to frame revenue exposure through FY24; it does not attempt to estimate claim severity or timing.

Apex FY22 is now expected to close at approximately $71.0M, versus the $96.0M peak in FY20. The decline began before the June cup recall in the underlying order data. The more pronounced step-down follows the September 2021 labeling update and what Sales characterizes as increased surgeon caution after the NJR data circulated. The recall remains a separate, lot-specific assumption in the model, although several field teams report customers are not making that distinction.

Summary output ($M):

| Scenario | FY22E | FY23E | FY24E | FY22–FY24 Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Status quo / current label | 71.0 | 62.4 | 60.1 | (15%) |
| Label-driven decline | 71.0 | 54.7 | 45.9 | (35%) |
| Full market withdrawal | 71.0 | 48.3 | 42.6 | (40%) |

The status quo case assumes current labeling remains in place, no broad commercial action, and modest attrition offset by existing account utilization. It is the closest to the current Sales operating plan, though I would not characterize it as the base case with high confidence.

The label-driven decline case assumes continued loss of new implanters, lower utilization among accounts that have moved Apex to a limited-use position, and increasing price concessions where distributors seek to retain volume. This case reflects the present trajectory in the Southeast and selected Midwest accounts more closely than the operating plan.

The withdrawal case assumes no new commercial placements after an orderly market action, with only limited residual revenue from contracted inventory and replacement requirements. This is necessarily a planning construct, not a recommendation regarding product status.

For reserve adequacy testing, I recommend using the full withdrawal scenario as the conservative revenue sensitivity. It produces the lowest contribution available to absorb claims-related costs and avoids relying on a recovery in surgeon confidence that we are not seeing in the current forecast submissions.

I have kept the $18M Q3 reserve as a separate line item in the workbook and have not assumed any insurance recoveries. We can walk through the account-level assumptions Monday if helpful.

Hannah

MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs; Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling; Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer
FROM: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
DATE: May 20, 2021
SUBJECT: Interim Registry Comparison & AJRR Preliminary Signal Synthesis — ApexHip

The purpose of this memo is to synthesize emerging clinical data regarding the ApexHip system across national registry datasets, internal post-market quality reporting, and historical biomechanical testing.

As the team is aware, the National Joint Registry (NJR) 17th Annual Report released in March flagged a cumulative 5-year revision rate for the ApexHip construct of 7.1% (95% CI: 5.8%–8.6%). By comparison, the broader contemporary metal-on-metal (MoM) class average in the registry sits at 3.2% at the 5-year mark, while ceramic-on-polyethylene benchmarks remain below 2.0%. This represents a statistically significant divergent hazard ratio that cannot be attributed solely to patient demographic outliers or surgical volume variance.

While official, validated data from the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) will not be formally published until late 2021, I have obtained an informal data preview through working-group contacts on the AJRR analytics subcommittee. The US dataset encompasses approximately 1,840 identified ApexHip implants tracked between 2017 and year-end 2020.

Although the US data remains unadjudicated, the preliminary curve mirrors the NJR cohort closely:
- At 3 years post-implantation, the preliminary AJRR data shows an all-cause revision rate of 4.4% for ApexHip, compared to an AJRR non-cemented MoM cohort average of 2.1%.
- Projecting the US Kaplan-Meier failure curve to 5 years yields an estimated revision rate between 6.8% and 7.4%, aligning almost exactly with the UK NJR’s 7.1%.
- Where revision indications are recorded in the US registry subset, mechanical loosening, pain of unexplained etiology, and local soft-tissue adverse reactions (ARMD/pseudotumor) account for over 65% of the re-operations.

This registry alignment must not be viewed in isolation. When mapped against our internal post-market data, the correlation is evident:
1. TrackWise Trending: Priya’s team has documented a persistent upward trend in metal-ion complaints and local adverse tissue reaction reports over the past six quarters, originating primarily from higher-volume early-adopter centers.
2. Biomechanical Testing: These clinical failure modes directly correlate with Tom Halvorsen’s February 2019 wear-test re-analysis (evaluating the acetabular component under edge-loading conditions at 55° cup inclination), which established a 4- to 6-fold increase in volumetric wear and resultant cobalt/chromium particle shedding relative to standard ISO 14242 45° parameters.

We are no longer looking at isolated regional artifacts. The convergence of Halvorsen's wear bench data, our rising internal TrackWise complaint logs, the confirmed NJR 7.1% revision benchmark, and the incoming AJRR preliminary signals demonstrate an established system-level trend.

Given these converging indicators, the cross-functional Registry Signal Review planned for September 2021 cannot simply note these findings as observational PMS monitoring. We must treat this as an active, convergent post-market safety signal and enter that session prepared to reach and formalize a binding, documented decision regarding risk mitigation, labeling revisions, and commercial status.

Date: June 5, 2023
From: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
To: File
Subject: Registry and complaint correlation memo - pre-MDL summary

This memorandum summarizes the relationship between external registry findings and Veridian’s internal ApexHip complaint and MDR trending through the current reporting period. I prepared this as a consolidated reference because we should expect requests for this material as the pending state-court matters develop and, potentially, are coordinated.

The short version is that the registry and complaint datasets have been directionally consistent since 2019. They are not interchangeable datasets, and neither proves causation on its own. However, both show a pattern of earlier-than-expected revision in a subset of ApexHip patients, with metal-ion findings, adverse local tissue reactions, and revision narratives that are consistent with a wear-related mechanism.

1. Registry findings

The March 2021 UK National Joint Registry annual report identified a five-year ApexHip revision rate of 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average for the relevant total-hip population. The NJR data have limitations: it does not provide complete patient-level laboratory values, surgeon technique variables are incompletely captured, and the product cohort is materially smaller than the aggregate comparator group. Nonetheless, the direction and magnitude of the difference warranted the September 2021 Registry Signal Review.

AJRR extracts received in late 2021 similarly showed an elevated revision signal for Apex relative to comparable contemporary total hips. The AJRR data were less mature than the NJR dataset at that time, and the confidence intervals were wider. The mid-2022 AJRR refresh did not eliminate the signal. Rather, it continued to show higher revision incidence in the Apex cohort, particularly in cases coded with pain, metallosis/metal-debris terminology, instability, or aseptic loosening. Coding practices vary by site, so these categories should not be treated as clinical adjudications.

2. Internal complaints and MDRs

TrackWise complaint entries first showed a meaningful cluster in 2018, including three metal-ion-related complaints from Atlanta-area patients treated in Dr. Feld’s practice. By 2019, the internal trend reports reflected increasing reports of elevated cobalt and chromium, pain, fluid collections, tissue reaction, and early revision. Not all reported cases contained complete records or confirmed implant component details. Several were initially coded under broad pain or revision categories before follow-up information was received.

The MDR population follows the same general trajectory. Reportable events increased as revisions and explant findings were received, although MDR timing should not be read as event timing because of reporting lags, supplemental records, and follow-up. The internal complaint/MDR trend is therefore most useful when reviewed by implant date and event date, where available, rather than filing date alone.

3. Mechanism assessment

The pattern is consistent with the edge-loading wear mechanism identified by Tom Halvorsen’s engineering team in the 2019 re-analysis of Apex wear testing. At 55-degree cup inclination, the testing showed approximately four- to six-fold increased wear relative to the standard 45-degree protocol. The clinical and registry data do not establish cup inclination for every affected patient, and patient, surgical, and implant variables may contribute. Still, elevated Co/Cr results and ARMD-type findings in the complaint records are directionally aligned with the engineering explanation and with the registry revision signal.

This conclusion is separate from the 2022 KinetiCoat cup-lot recall. The recalled V-2200 through V-2299 lots concern coating adhesion and a manufacturing parameter drift at Cork; they should not be combined analytically with the metal-ion/wear signal absent a case-specific basis.

Recommendation: Quality and PMS should finalize the Apex complaint database, including the current reconciliation of duplicate and follow-up records, and maintain a cross-reference between complaint/MDR records and the applicable NJR and AJRR citations. Any external response should clearly identify data-source limitations, reporting lags, and the distinction between the coating recall and the wear-related issue.

Following our discussion last week regarding the September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I asked Hannah Berg to help model out our potential downstream exposure. As we finalized the path to maintain ApexHip commercial distribution supported by a labeling update and the upcoming Dear Doctor advisory, we need to understand the financial parameters should the registry trends in the UK (NJR) and domestic tracking (AJRR) fail to stabilize over the next 12 to 24 months.

Please note that this analysis is strictly exploratory and does not reflect a formal accounting position or GAAP accrual.

Scenario Modeling (FY 2022–2024 Outlook)

Our projections hinge on two primary variables: continued commercial volume and actual cumulative revision divergence against historical class baselines. At our current run-rate (~14,000 systems annually at ~$9,800 ASP), a continued divergence toward the 7.1% 5-year revision rate flagged by the NJR introduces predictable indemnity and defense tailwinds.

| Scenario | Modeled Revision Uplift | Est. System Volume (3-Yr) | Potential Claims Exposure / Reserve Range |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Low Case | +1.5% to 2.0% over class average | 32,000 units (assumes tapering) | $8.0M – $11.5M |
| Mid Case | +3.0% to 3.5% over class average | 38,000 units (steady adoption) | $14.0M – $18.5M |
| High Case | +4.0%+ over class average | 42,000 units (aggressive growth) | $20.0M – $25.0M |

*Low Case* assumes our surgical technique labeling updates take hold, mitigating edge-loading outliers, with claims limited primarily to concentrated revisions and modest legal defense. *High Case* contemplates persistent ARMD and ion-related complications driving formal litigation across multiple territories, forcing substantial per-case settlements.

Recommendations

At present, ASC 450 (Contingencies) criteria for an accrual are not met; loss is neither probable nor reasonably estimable given the lack of active filed litigation and the uncertain causal link to technique versus manufacturing.

1. Maintain Current Stance: Do not book a formal balance sheet reserve for Q3 or FY21 year-end.
2. Quarterly Registry Monitoring: Finance should receive direct quarterly syntheses from Greg Novak's team to track NJR and AJRR curve inflections against these sensitivity bands.
